findings.claim: The menu's tag list does not drop tags that contain a quote character, although folders and collections are filtered with hasQuote.
findings.impact: A tag whose name starts with a quote is written as tag:"name, which the tokenizer reads as an open quoted value for a different tag, so the chip and the filter do not match the tag the user chose. This needs a tag name containing a quote, which is rare.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/search/SearchQueryHeader.tsx:207-214: tagOptions comes from suggestValues with no hasQuote filter, while folderOptions and collectionOptions filter with hasQuote. The spec (item 6) says a value containing a quote is not offered by the menu.

bucket_proposal.reason: I9 and I11 name folders and collections only, so no declared invariant is broken. The behaviour is inconsistent with spec item 6.

findings.proposed_fix: Filter tag options with hasQuote, as the other two lists do.

findings.claim: The frontend trims collection names with JS trim() and lowercases with toLowerCase(), while the core uses Python strip() and lower(). The two differ for a few exotic characters.
findings.impact: A collection value with a character such as U+FEFF or a control separator may be accepted by the parser but be trimmed differently, or be deduplicated differently, by the core. The two sides could then produce a different count or set of names. This is a corner case that normal personal use does not reach.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/lib/searchQuery.ts normaliseCollection uses value.trim() and interpret uses toLowerCase(). backend/app/routers/drives.py normalize_collections uses raw.strip() and name.lower().

bucket_proposal.reason: I10 says the parser turns into text every value the server would reject. This differs only on exotic whitespace and case-folding characters, and the threat model puts crafted input out of scope.

specification_compliance: I1/I2/I3/I4: apply_file_filters is shared by the listing and /files/matching. The folder test is exact-or-prefix-plus-slash via substr, which is case-sensitive. Collections are resolved only from Collection.drive == drive with a Python lower() comparison. These match the invariants as read.

I7/I10: both surfaces use the shared normalize_folders and normalize_collections. The addon SearchFilter duplicates the logic with the same rules, and extra=forbid is set on both models. The caps count after dedupe on both.
I5/I12/I13: parse, chips and removal all go through interpret/tokenize. closeOpenQuote adds the closing quote only when the last token is open.
I14: the chip uses min-w-0, max-w-full, ellipsis and a shrink-0 ✕, backed by an e2e-layout fixture. I did not run it.
regression_risks: apply_file_filters raises ValueError when collections is given without drive. Both callers in the diff pass drive.
extra=forbid on FileMatchingRequest rejects any future caller that sends an unknown key. This is intended by the spec.
test_coverage: The two fix commits only add tests: cap-after-dedupe, case-variant folders, other-drive collection, ß folding, trailing-letter trimming, chip removal and mixed quotes. These pin the earlier mutants.

The test row named 'a longer sibling name is not the folder' repeats the exact-folder row, and the row named 'the drive root is not a folder value' asserts Café. These are naming issues only, and the cases they should cover are covered by other tests.
The ten-folder and ten-collection disabled-menu state is tested. I did not see a test that the tag list hides tags containing a quote.
not_verified: I ran no tests, mutations or the browser layout test.

trajectory: The two fix commits only add tests and move the addon pointer to the commit with the killing tests. Neither adds a branch, state or prediction to production code. No round adds a branch the previous round also added, and no round removes one. This is not patching of the design.
